casuallab.title: Known-truth HTE benchmark
casuallab.question: Who should get the offer?
casuallab.method: I test effect estimates against known answers, then compare spending rules at the same budget in simulated markets held out from training.
casuallab.finding: The complex targeting model has not earned its advantage. The learner misses the recovery benchmark. In the budget experiment, a uniform allocation also produces more incremental trips than the model-based rule.
casuallab.note: Semi-synthetic validation, not a measured effect of a real NYC promotion. The oracle knows the true average effect; it is a test benchmark, not a deployable policy.
casuallab.chart_caption: Lower RMSE is better; the learner must beat the oracle.

macroeconomics.title: Leakage-safe real-time backtest
macroeconomics.question: Would the forecast work in real time?

headline.label: future information cells in strict as-of

macroeconomics.method: I reconstruct official release histories and rerun forecasts with three information rules: data known then, revised values with the same availability, and unrestricted latest values.
macroeconomics.finding: Changing the data vintage changes which models look best. Only the strict as-of rule avoids both future releases and future revisions. Even holding availability fixed, revised values change the GDP ranking of all six models.
macroeconomics.note: The fixed-mask comparison is a hindsight diagnostic, not a valid real-time forecast. Results describe this pilot and its final holdout; they do not establish a universally best model.
macroeconomics.chart_caption: Strict as-of and fixed mask both exclude future first releases. Fixed mask still uses later revisions; switch to the revisions metric to see them.

metrics.label: Later revisions
metrics.caption: Only strict as-of excludes later revisions. Fixed mask contains 5,464 and naive revised contains 6,311 cells selected from after the forecast date.

metrics.label: Missing
metrics.caption: Missing cells: 299 under strict as-of and fixed mask, versus 225 under unrestricted latest data. Extra completeness can itself reflect unavailable future information.

realestate.title: Mortgage lock-in profile
realestate.question: Does a cheap mortgage keep a loan in place?

headline.label: hazard ratio per +1 pp rate gap

realestate.method: I compare monthly payoff rates across rate gaps, then estimate a complementary log-log hazard model with observed loan and local-market controls.
realestate.finding: Larger rate gaps are associated with lower exit hazards. The complementary log-log model reports a 0.817 hazard ratio per +1 percentage point.
realestate.note: Association only. Payoff and maturity are pooled; refinancing-related and sale-related payoffs cannot be distinguished. Household moves are not observed. Raw shares are from an exit-enriched sample.
realestate.chart_caption: Unweighted exit shares in a sample that overrepresents exiting loans; these are not population monthly probabilities. The 0.817 hazard ratio comes from the separate adjusted complementary log-log model.

microstructure.title: Signal-to-execution stress test
microstructure.question: How much short-horizon edge does order flow carry?
microstructure.method: I replay one four-hour BTC/ETH order-book capture across two evaluation phases, four horizons, and nine delay combinations, with a fixed 4 bp fee.
microstructure.finding: Order flow carries a positive gross edge in 110 of 144 execution scenarios. The best gross edge reaches 2.39 bp, measured against a fixed 4 bp taker fee; lower-cost execution is the next test.
microstructure.note: Exploratory simulation · research reference only · not live trading. The 144 scenarios overlap and are not independent experiments or a portfolio to add together.
microstructure.chart_caption: Min, median, and max across 144 counterfactual scenarios; do not sum.

tariff-incidence.title: Tariff incidence decomposition
tariff-incidence.question: Who absorbed the tariff?
tariff-incidence.method: I compare each wave of tariffed products with never-tariffed products, tracking unit import values before and after the policy and checking three sample windows.
tariff-incidence.finding: The evidence points toward higher costs for U.S. importers. Unit values before duty show no clear offsetting decline. Duty-inclusive unit values rise. This pattern supports importer-side incidence within the sample.
tariff-incidence.note: Unit values are not individual transaction prices. The duty-inclusive measure includes the tariff by construction; the pre-duty series is essential. Quantity fails its date-placebo check.
tariff-incidence.chart_caption: Pre-duty unit values are near +0.025 log points. Dashed bounds (±0.076) are effect bounds, not confidence intervals.

metrics.label: Including duty
metrics.caption: Duty-inclusive unit values rise by about 0.15 log points; the dashed line is the mechanical tariff reference, not a confidence interval.

metrics.label: Import quantity
metrics.caption: The quantity series fails its date-placebo test. Its decline must not be presented as a clean causal tariff effect.

em-factor-timing.title: Emerging-market factor timing & transfer
em-factor-timing.question: Can machine learning time equity factors?

headline.label: shrinkage-mean OOS R² vs own mean

em-factor-timing.method: I compare out-of-sample linear, tree, and neural-network forecasts on JKP global factors, test developed-to-emerging-market transfer, and evaluate timing after turnover costs.
em-factor-timing.finding: Pooling explains much of the apparent predictability. On capped value-weighted factors, all learned forecasts lose to the shrinkage mean on out-of-sample R², and the shrinkage-mean tilt achieves the highest net Sharpe (1.91).
em-factor-timing.note: Out-of-sample predictive association. Results depend on factor weighting and trading costs; equal-weighted factors differ. Factor returns exclude their own rebalancing costs.
em-factor-timing.chart_caption: Against the unpooled own mean, every model has positive OOS R² (+0.73% to +1.16%), but the non-timing shrinkage mean alone reaches +1.20% (t = 9.05).

metrics.label: OOS R² vs shrinkage mean
metrics.caption: Measured against the regional shrinkage mean, all 12 learned model-scope combinations have negative OOS R² (−0.05% to −0.48%) due to forecast over-dispersion.

metrics.label: Net Sharpe (20 bp)
metrics.caption: At 20 bp per unit of turnover, the shrinkage-mean tilt (1.91) beats static equal weight (1.48) and every learned timing portfolio (0.71–1.26).

series.outcome: best learned net Sharpe at 20 bp

polymarket-factors.title: Prediction-market artifact & factor audit
polymarket-factors.question: Which prediction-market signals survive a realistic backtest?
polymarket-factors.method: I study 4,000 Polymarket markets, remove five backtest artifacts, control for price levels, and evaluate factor signs on a held-out half of the panel.
polymarket-factors.finding: Reversal, volatility, and illiquidity survive the corrections. Five backtest artifacts inflate 30-day momentum IC eightfold (−0.440 to −0.054); price-neutral OOS ICs remain significant for illiquidity (−0.072), volatility (−0.069), and reversal (−0.032).
polymarket-factors.note: Backtest association, not live execution. Capacity is roughly $100–200 per position. The combined strategy weight was chosen in sample, and daily-close fills omit intraday slippage.
polymarket-factors.chart_caption: Out-of-sample price-neutral IC (residualized on [1, p, p²]) across 54 five-day evaluation periods (2025-06-28 to 2026-03-20).

metrics.label: Raw Δp IC (OOS)
metrics.caption: Without residualizing on [1, p, p²], spread (+0.047) and extremity (+0.044) appear stronger because they ride mechanical boundary skewness.

crypto-factors.title: Cross-market factor transfer & post-publication OOS
crypto-factors.question: Do equity microstructure factors travel to crypto?
crypto-factors.method: I test cross-sectional factors on 105 coins, check split samples and parameters, compare funding on OKX, and track the composite after publication.
crypto-factors.finding: Most factors do not travel; funding (+1.42 Sharpe), retail positioning (+1.39), and low-price range (+1.63) hold up in the 730-day panel, while post-publication windows (June–August 2026) returned −6.5% without re-fitting.
crypto-factors.note: Backtest and out-of-sample backtest association, not live trading. Next-close fills omit market impact; the sample is an altcoin bear market and the OKX check is short.
crypto-factors.chart_caption: 730-day daily quintile long–short Sharpe (net of 5 bp/side) across 105 coins on Binance spot and perpetuals.
